model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for several model variants. The x-axis represents "#Iteration" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000 with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents "Loss" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1.

Six lines are shown, all starting at high loss values near 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreasing steeply during the first ~20,000 iterations before gradually leveling off. The "Vanilla" line (light purple/lavender, solid) decreases from approximately 3.4 to around 2.50–2.52 by iteration 140,000, placing it among the lowest final loss values. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" line (blue, solid) follows a similar initial descent but plateaus at a noticeably higher loss, ending at approximately 2.62 by iteration 140,000, making it the highest-loss curve at the end. The "SepLLM (n=64)" line (orange, solid) tracks closely with the Vanilla line and reaches approximately 2.52–2.53 by iteration 140,000. The "SepLLM (n=64, H)" line (green, solid) behaves very similarly to the SepLLM (n=64) line, ending near 2.51–2.52. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" line (red, solid) also closely overlaps with the Vanilla and other SepLLM variants, reaching approximately 2.50–2.52 at iteration 140,000. The "SepLLM (n=128)" line (dark blue/navy, solid) follows a trajectory slightly above the StrmLLM line for much of the training, ending at approximately 2.60–2.62 by iteration 140,000. All lines exhibit some visible noise or fluctuation throughout training, particularly the StrmLLM and SepLLM (n=128) lines, which remain distinctly above the cluster of lower-loss curves from roughly iteration 20,000 onward.
